payload.title: What Are the Japanese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Japanese wedding traditions in wedding order, from yuinō and the Shinto ceremony with san-san-kudo to the shiromuku, the hirōen, goshūgi and kagami biraki, with notes for Australians marrying in Japan or at home.
key_takeaways: A traditional Japanese wedding often pairs a Shinto ceremony in kimono with a Christian-style ceremony in Western dress on the same day.
The bride's white shiromuku belongs to the ceremony, and a change into a coloured kimono, or a Western gown, marks her return for the reception.
Guests give goshūgi, a gift of money in a formal envelope, and leave with hikidemono, the gifts the couple give in return.
For Australians marrying in Japan, Smartraveller advises normal safety precautions, and the legal steps are confirmed with the municipal office and the Australian Embassy.

faq.q: What happens at a traditional Japanese wedding?
faq.a: A Shinto ceremony in kimono, typically followed by a Christian-style observance in Western dress, then the hirōen reception with speeches, a change of outfits and the bride's letter to her parents.
The sharing of sake from three cups by the bride and groom during a Shinto wedding, and at many weddings by their parents too.

faq.q: What is the Japanese wedding kimono called?
faq.a: The bride's white ceremony kimono is the shiromuku. For the reception she changes into a brightly coloured outer kimono, the iro-uchikake.

faq.q: What gifts do guests give at a Japanese wedding?
faq.a: Guests give goshūgi, money in a formal envelope tied with mizuhiki cords, handed in at the reception desk.
The gifts the couple give each guest to take home, often a main gift with a sweet beside it.

faq.q: What should guests wear to a Japanese wedding?
faq.a: Formal dress. Women often wear a cocktail dress or formal kimono and avoid all-white, which belongs to the bride; men wear a dark suit. Ask the couple if the shrine has its own guidance.

faq.q: Can Australians have a legal wedding in Japan?
faq.a: In most cases, yes: an overseas marriage is legally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. Check documents and fees with the municipal office and the Australian Embassy in Tokyo.
